AI Page Builder

Describe it — AI builds the page for you

No blank-page stress. Tell the AI what your page is about and it drafts the headline, description, button, theme colour and feature cards — straight into the builder, ready for you to fine-tune, add ads and publish. AI follows your description strictly: it builds only what you describe and adds nothing extra — no invented features, sections or claims.

  1. 1Pick a ready prompt or describe your page — tap a suggestion for a restaurant, portfolio, shop, gym, salon, course, event or service business and it fills the box for you, or write your own: what it sells or offers, who it is for, and what the button should do.
  2. 2AI drafts it in the builder — only what your description asks for: headline, text, button and theme colour, applied to the live preview. Feature cards are made only if your description mentions features — if it doesn't, none are added.
  3. 3Fine-tune & publish — change anything, add ad codes in the Ads tab, then publish with a public link.

Publish your page in one place

No separate hosting and no file to upload. Finish your design in the builder, choose a short page address, and press Publish — you get one full public link for the page. Anyone who opens that link, in any browser on any phone or computer, sees your finished page with your ads: phone visitors get the mobile design, computer visitors get the desktop design, from the same link. Visitors see only your page — never the builder.

Separate device design

Desktop and mobile are designed separately. Switch the preview device (top-right of the preview) and adjust each version — visitors automatically see the design made for their device.

Drag to place — position by hand

Turn on Drag to Place above the preview, then press and drag any text, image, button, feature card, block or ad block to its perfect place. Positions are saved separately for Desktop and Mobile: set the Desktop positions, switch the preview to Mobile, and drag again for the phone version. Fine-tune or reset any element from its click-to-edit panel.

Build your page block by block — this is how a Blank Page is made. Blocks appear below your hero section in order. You can also click a block in the preview to edit it.

Ads are managed in the Ads tab. The fixed slots and the Custom Ad blocks that can sit anywhere in your content — including any ad blocks already on this page — are all added, edited and positioned from the Ads tab, so every ad job happens in one place. Ad blocks still show in the list below so you can see the content order, and Up / Down still moves them.

Every ad on this page is managed here, in one place — the same ad system a Blank Page is built with: six fixed slots, plus Custom Ad blocks you can place anywhere in your content. Paste codes from Adsterra or any other network. Nothing ad-related lives in the Blocks tab any more.

Paste the code exactly as your network gives it

  1. Create the ad unit in your network dashboard first (Adsterra: Websites → your site → Add Ad Unit).
  2. Copy the FULL HTML code — every <script> tag and everything around it, exactly as given, in the same order. Do not shorten it, and do not paste only a link or only an image.
  3. Paste it into a slot below, or into a Custom Ad placed anywhere in your content.
  4. Publish, then open the live page to test. Ad code runs on the published live page — never inside this builder preview, which protects your account from invalid self-impressions.

What full Adsterra code looks like: a banner or native unit is usually an inline <script> that sets its options (often starting atOptions = { 'key' : … }) followed by a second <script src="…/invoke.js"> tag; a Popunder or Social Bar code is usually a single <script src="…"> tag. Paste all of it — the published page runs it exactly as pasted, script tags included. One code per slot or block; never paste the same code twice, and never click your own ads.

Hide ad names — the published page shows only the ad

Visitors never need to see the word "Ad", a slot name or a network name. Turn this on and your published page shows only the ad that your code loads — no label, no heading, no network name above or below it. The names you see in this tab are private builder labels for you only. The ad keeps working exactly the same, because it runs from the code, not from the name.

This applies to every slot below and to every Custom Ad block you place anywhere on the page.

Ad slots — fixed positions on every page

Pick the slot that matches the place you want — Popunder, Top Banner, In-Content, Native, Social Bar or Sticky Footer — then paste that unit's full code into it.

Custom Ads — place an ad anywhere in your content

The slots above are fixed positions. A Custom Ad is a block inside your content itself — between two paragraphs, after a heading, before a button, at the very top or the very end. Add one, paste its full code, then set its exact place with Up / Down in the list below, or drag it by hand in Drag Mode above the preview.

Publish & host on PageCraft

No separate hosting, no file upload. Pressing Publish packs your finished page — text, image, buttons, layout, drag positions and ad codes — into a public link on this domain. Anyone who opens that full link, in any browser, on any phone or computer, sees the page exactly as you designed it. Visitors see only the page — never the builder, never an editor.

/p/
Public URLAnyone can open it — no login needed to view
/p/my-page

This is your page's address name. Press Publish and the full public link appears in your browser's address bar, ready to copy and share; its ending — the part that carries the page — is also kept in My Pages. Phone visitors see your mobile design, computer visitors see your desktop design, automatically, and your ads run there too, with ad names hidden if you turned that on in the Ads tab.

Every published page also lives in My Pages — open it, copy its link, edit it or unpublish it there, any time.

What “public” means here

Your finished page travels inside its public link (compressed into the link's ending), so the link works everywhere by itself: another person, another browser, another device — everyone opens the same page, with the design for their screen and the ads loaded by your codes, and with no ad names or network names shown when Hide Ad Names is on. Always share the full link — this site's web address plus the link ending Publish gives you (after publishing, the full link is sitting in your browser's address bar). The short /p/your-page-name address on its own only opens in this browser, where the page was published. If you change the page later, press Publish again to get a refreshed link; the old link keeps showing the version it was made from.

Hosted only: PageCraft templates and pages can't be downloaded as files — publishing here creates the public link that carries the page live on this domain.
